case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated May 9, 2001 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3560 of 1993)
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J : This appeal, by leave, is by the heirs of defendant No. 1 against the judgment dated May 9, 2001 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3560 of 1993 making absolute the Rule obtained against the Judgment and decree dated November 17, 1993 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Barisal in Title Appeal No. 67 of 1985 allowing the same and thereby dismissing the suit upon reversing the judgment and decree dated April 28, 1985 of the Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge) Upazila Babuganj, Barisal in Title Suit No. 285 of 1984 decreeing the same in part and thereby declaring title of the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 acquired by the kabala dated September 30, 1975 and also declaring title of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to have been acquired by adverse possession in respect of the part of the land in suit and that further declaring the judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 void and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

2. The suit was filed seeking primarily the reliefs which are:

(ক) বিরোধীয় (খ)তফছিল বর্ণিত ডিক্রি ভাক্ত, ফেরবী ও nul and void  সাব্যস্থে তাহা রহিত ও বাদীয়গণ প্রতি বাধ্যকর না থাকা মর্মে ঘোষনা মূলক ডিক্রি দিবার।

(খ)বিরোধীয় (গ)তফছিল বর্ণিত ভূমিতে বাদীগণের রায়তি স্বত্ব থাকা মর্মে ঘোষনা মূলক ডিক্রি দিবার। Schedule 'Kha' to the plaint is as follows :

(খ) তপছিল বিরোধীয় ডিক্রি মোঃ বরিশালের ২য় মুন্সেফি আদালত দেং মোঃ ২০৬/৭৬ এরশেদ আলী হাওলাদার গং-বনাম-আশ্বিনী কুমার গং-বাদী। -বিবাদী।

রুজুঃ-১১-৩-৭৬

তায়দাদঃ- ৩০০০/০০

ছোলে সুত্রে ডিক্রির তাং ২০/৬/৭৬

And Schedule 'Ga' to the plaint is as follows:

(গ) তপছিল

জিঃ বাখরগঞ্জ ষ্টেশন বাবুগঞ্জ অধীন জে, এল, ৩৫ নং তেহেরগতি মৌজায় এস, এ ৬০ নং খতিয়ানের ৫১১৯/৫৯২০/৫৯২৭/৫৯২৮/৫৯২৯/৫৯৩০/৫৯৫৮/ দাগে জমি ২.২৩ শঃ।

ষ্টেশন মৌজা ঐ এস, এ, ১২৮২ নং খতিয়ানের ৫৯৪২ দাগের হিং। এস, এ, ১২৮৩ নং খতিয়ানের ৫৯৫১ দাগের হিং। আনী এস, এ, ১২৮৪ নং খতিয়ানের ৫৯৩৯ দাগের। ।০ এস, এ, ১২৮৫ নং খতিয়ানের ৫৯৫৩ দাগের হিং। ।০ আনী, এস, এ, ১২৮৬ নং খতিয়ানের ৫৯৩৭ দাগের হিং। /৬।।// মোট জমি ২.২৩+.৩৮= ২.৬১ শতাংশ।

3. It may be mentioned the land as in schedule 'Ga' is part of the land described in schedule 'Ka' which is as follows:

জিলা বাখরগঞ্জ অধীন ষ্টেশন বাবুগঞ্জ অন্তর্গত ৩৫ নং জে, এল, দেহেরগতি মৌজায় হাল ৫৯২০ দাগের হিং।। আনা এবং হাল ৫৯১৯/৫৯২৯/৫৯৩০ নং দাগের হিং ১ আনী এবং হাল ৫৯১৯/৫৯২৯/৫৯৩০ নং দাগের হিং ১ আনী এবং হাল ৫৯৫৮ নং দাগের হিং//০ আনী এবং হাল ৫৯৪৫/৫৯৪৬/৫৯৪৭ নং দাগের হিং।। ১৩ ক্রান্তি অংশে ২.৮১ শতাংশ ভূমির তৎকালীন মালিক পত্তন দাতা ১-৯ নং বিবাদীগণের নিকট হইতে বিগত ১৩৫১ সনের মাঘ মাসের ১৫ তারিখে পত্তন মুলে বার্ষিক মং ১০ টাকা জমায় আপোষ মতে মালিক দাখিলকার ২নং বাদী যাহা রিভিশনাল জরিপের ১৮২৬/১/২৪৩৯ তথা এস, এ, ৬০/৭২ নং খতিয়ানে পরিমিত হইয়াছে।

২। জিলা ষ্টেঃ মৌজা জে, এল, ঐ মধ্যে হাল ৫৯৪২/৫৯৫১/৫৯৩৯/৫৯৫৩ নং দাগের //০ আনী এবং হাল ৫৯৩৭ নং দাগের হিং ।/৬।// ক্রান্তি অংশে যথাক্রমে ৩৮ শতাংশে ভূমির তৎকালীন পত্তন দাতা ১৩/১১ নং বিবাদীগনের নিকট হইতে বিগত ১৩৫১ সনের মাঘ মাসের ১৫ তারিখে বার্ষিক ২ ।।০ আনা জমায় আপোষ মতে মালিক দাখিলকার ২ নং বাদী যাহা রিভিশনাল জরিপে ১৮১৬/২,২৯৮৯/২৬৬/২৪৬/২৭৪৫ তথা এস, এ, ১২৮২/১২৮৩/১২৮৫/১২৮৬ নং খতিয়ানের পরিমিত হইয়াছে।

4. It was the case of the plaintiffs that defendant Nos. 1-6 and defendant Nos. 8-11 of Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 died long before the institution of the said suit, that plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 4-6 of the instant suit i.e. Title Suit No. 285 of 1984, are the heirs of defendant Nos.1-6 of Title Suit No. 206 of 1976, that plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 4-6 got their names mutated on March 10, 1969 and that plaintiff No. 1 and defendant Nos. 4-6 each having 8 annas share, that defendant Nos. 4-6 sold their share to the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 on September 30, 1975, that defendant Nos.1 and 2 of the instant suit i.e. Title Suit No. 285 of 1984, although had no title but they instituted Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 seeking declaration of their title impleading the plaintiff No. 1 and the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 4-6 of the instant suit upon giving wrong address and thereupon, suppressing summonses obtained degree fraudulently in respect of the land of the plaintiff No.1 and defendant Nos. 4-6 of the instant suit, that the plaintiffs or their predecessors did not settle the land in suit to the defendants, that the plaintiffs came to know about the fraudulent decree obtained by the defendant Nos.1 and 2 in Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 on 15-10-1976 and that upon obtaining the information supplied by the Court on 12-11-1976 became certain about the fraudulent decree obtained by the defendant Nos.1 and 2 in Title Suit No. 206 of 1976. Hence the suit.

5. The suit was contested by defendant No. 1 by filing written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint and also contending that the suit was barred by limitation. The definite case of the defendant No. 1 is that the plaintiff case that defendant Nos. 1-6 and 8-11 of Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 died before filing of the same is not correct, that plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 4-6 of the instant suit are not the heirs of the defendant Nos. 1-6 and 8-11 of Title Suit No. 206 of 1976, that defendant Nos. 4-6 had no interest in the land described in schedule 'Ga' and that defendant Nos.1 and 2 got the land by settlement and are in possession thereof, that summonses of Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 were duly served on the defendants, that defendant Nos.1 and 2 of the instant suit got the land by settlement from the defendants of the Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 on 15th March, 1351 BS and since then the defendants are enjoying the land so got by settlement, that defendants of the Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 and the plaintiff No. 1 of the instant suit entered appearance in Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 upon engaging an Advocate and they filed solenama, and on the basis of the said solenama the suit was decreed, that the solenama so filed was quite genuine, that the plaintiffs have filed the suit making untrue statements.

6. The trial Court decreed the suit on the finding that the suit is not had for defect of party and that summonses of Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 were suppressed and thereupon decree was obtained, that defendants failed to dislodge the contention of the plaintiffs that defendant Nos.1-6 and 8-11 of Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 died before the institution thereof, that the defendant Nos.1 and 2 in the instant suit obtained decree in Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 against dead persons, that the document of the .plaintiff Nos. 2-4 by which they have purchased the land claimed by them as in schedule 'Ga' from defendant Nos. 4-6 of the instant suit is genuine and the said plaintiffs are in possession, that defendants failed to establish their case of taking oral settlement of the land in suit and that their story of taking settlement orally is a get-up story, that defendant No. 2 is in possession of part of the land in suit, that defendants have acquired title by adverse possession as regard the land of plaintiff No. 1.

7. On appeal by the defendant No. 1 the appellate Court reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the finding that the suit as framed was not maintainable since the evidence on record shows that the defendants are in possession of the land in suit and, as such, plaintiffs were required to seek declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. The appellate Court also observed that trial Court was in error in decreeing the suit in part i.e. decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff Nos. 2-4. The appellate Court further held that the document on the basis of which plaintiff Nos. 2-4 were claiming the land in suit is not genuine since the signature of the executants of the kabala and the signature of the identifier of the said kabala is of the same hand. It was also noticed by the appellate Court that the PWs 2 and 3 admitted possession of the land in suit by the defendants. It may be mentioned it was the contention of the appellant that the suit framed is not maintainable since the land in suit is unspecified and description of the land claimed by the plaintiffs is vague, in that there is no statement that plaintiffs are in possession of which part of the land of the suit plots as mentioned in schedule 'Ga'. The appellate Court upon allowing the appeal set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and thereupon dismissed the suit.

8. As against the judgment and decree of the appellate Court the plaintiff No. 3 alone moved the High Court, Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the finding that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 was obtained without serving summonses on the defendants, that the judgment of the appellate Court has been passed without adverting to the Exhibits 2-4 and that the finding of the appellate Court as to genuineness of the Exhibit, i.e. the kabala, on the basis of which plaintiff Nos. 2-4 were claiming the land in suit which they are said to have purchased from defendant Nos. 4-6 of the instant suit is not correct since land claimed by the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 was transferred by the elder brother on behalf of his minor brothers, that the trial Court was in error in passing a decree in respect of the land claimed by plaintiffs in favour of defendant Nos.1 and 2 who said to have acquired title thereof by adverse possession, that the trial Court in the background of which materials declared the title of the defendant Nos.1 and 2 in part of the land in suit said to have acquired said title by adverse possession was under the law required to dismiss the suit, that appellate Court while setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court did not advert itself to the evidence on record and that did not reverse the finding and decision of the trial Court. It has also been held by the High Court Division that the appellate Court while setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court did not reverse the finding of the trial Court as regard the decree i.e. the compromise decree, obtained in Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 and that the appellate Court was in error by discarding the Exhibit 1 i.e. kabala, on the basis of which plaintiff Nos. 2-4 claimed half of the land of 'Ga' schedule comprising the entire land in suit and as to which declaration of title has been sought.

9. Leave was granted to consider the contention that the plaintiff Nos.1-4 filed the suit seeking declaration of title in respect of 2.61 acres of land and the Courts below found that the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 are in possession of 8 annas share of the land in suit and the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are in possession of the rest 8 annas share of the plaintiff No. 1 and that the plaintiff No. 1 is out of possession of the land in suit and thereupon decreed the suit in part, but the land in suit as claimed by the plaintiff No. 1 as well as by the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 are not specified or, in other words, was not shown separately in the schedule of the plaint, and without specification of the share of the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 as the mere declaratory decree cannot be sustainable in law which was passed by the trial Court and restored by the High Court Division and that the High Court Division was in serious error in not noticing the fact that the plaintiffs are out of possession of the land in suit and, as such, without the prayer for consequential relief the suit seeking simple declaration of title was not maintainable.

10. The learned Advocate-on-Record in support of the appeal reiterated the contention making which leave was obtained.

<u>11. The respondent No. 1 i.e. petitioner, before the High Court Division in the revisional application entered appearance through the learned Advocate-on-Record but did not file concise statement. The learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the respondent No. 1 submitted that the learned Senior Counsel would make submission in the appeal for the respondent No. 1 and the learned Counsel who would make submission on behalf of the respondent No. 1 at the moment is not available and, in that state of the matter, the learned Advocate-on-Record when called upon to make submission he did not make any submission on behalf of the respondent No. 1. It may be mentioned since no concise statement was filed under the Rules of the Appellate Division, the Advocate-on-Record for the respondent No. 1 or the learned Counsel, who as submitted by the learned Advocate on Record, would have made submission for the respondent had no right of making submission on behalf of the respondent No. 1.</u>

12. It is seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that the said Division while setting aside the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court did not address itself to the question of maintainability of the suit, particularly because of the fact that the trial Court decreed the suit in part in respect of unspecified land and that the relief sought as regard the land described in schedule 'Ga' to the plaint being declaration simpliciter although because of the evidence of PWs 2 and 3 it was found by the primary Court of fact as well as by the last Court of fact that the plaintiff No. 1 is not in possession of the land of 'Ga' Schedule part of which, not specified, claimed by him along with plaintiff Nos. 2-4.

13. In the afore state of the matter the High Court Division was in error in reversing the judgment and decree of the appellate Court and thereupon restoring the judgment and decree of the trial Court when one of the plaintiffs is out of the possession of the land in suit and that there is no specification in which particular part of the plots in suit which particular plaintiff or plaintiffs are in possession.

14. The suit was filed seeking declaration in respect of 2 matters, one of which is, that the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 was null and void and the other, relief was for declaration of title of the plaintiffs in respect of the land described in schedule 'Ga' attached to the plaint. It may be mentioned land of schedule 'Ga' is part of the land described in schedule 'Ka' attached to the plaint. The plaintiffs, in all 4, sought for declaration of title in respect of the land measuring 2.61 acres described in schedule 'Ga' attached to the plaint. It was averred in the plaint that plaintiff No. 1 is the owner of the half of the land in suit and the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 are the owners of the half of the land in suit. There is nothing in the plaint to show which particular half of the land of the plots mentioned in schedule 'Ga' is possessed by the plaintiff No. 1 and which other part of the land of the said plots are being possessed by the plaintiff Nos. 2-4. As stated hereinbefore, that trial Court on due consideration of the evidence on record arrived at the finding that of the plaintiffs, the plaintiff No. 1 is not in possession of the land claimed by him and that land claimed by the plaintiff No. 1 is being possessed by the defendant No. 2 from the schedule 'Ka' and 'Ga' (as mentioned hereinbefore) where land in suit claimed by the plaintiffs have been described it is seen that the plaintiffs are not claiming the entire land of the plots mentioned in schedule 'Ga' to the plaint and on the top of that, as has already been mentioned PWs 2 and 3 have admitted that defendant Nos.1 and 2 are in possession of the land in suit claimed by the plaintiff No. 1. The suit, being a simple declaratory one, on the face of the materials on record was not maintainable since plaintiffs being out of possession were required to seek for consequential relief i.e. recovery of possession along with the prayer for declaration of title, but the plaintiffs have prayed for mere declaration of title. The appellate Court while setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court noticed this particular material fact that plaintiff No. 1 is out of possession of the land in suit and that there is no specification of the land claimed by the plaintiffs, particularly by plaintiff Nos. 2-4 and thus the trial Court in passing the part decree in favour of the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 was in error or, in other words, the decree passed by the trial Court was not a legal one and thereupon set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The High Court Division while interfering with the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court was quite unmindful of the fact that of the 4 plaintiffs, who are claiming the land of schedule 'Ga' jointly, since there was no specification which particular half is being possessed by which plaintiff or plaintiffs, sought for declaration of title and that in the background of the evidence on record it was found by the Court i.e. the Court of first instance, that part of the land in suit claimed by the plaintiff No. 1 is in possession of the defendant Nos.1 and 2 and thereupon, decreed the suit in part in favour of the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 but being unmindful of the fact there is no specification of the land claimed by the plaintiff No. 1 and the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 and it appears from the averments made in the plaint that the plaintiffs, in all 4, are in joint possession of the land of the plots as mentioned in schedule 'Ga' to the plaint. It also appears from the schedule 'Ka' and 'Ga' that plaintiffs are not claiming the entire land of the plots mentioned in the second part of the schedule 'Ga'.

<u>15. Plaintiff for the purpose of success in his suit and thereupon to have the relief sought in the suit is required first, to establish that the suit as framed is maintainable and that when the Court finds that the suit is maintainable then goes for consideration of the claim of the plaintiff(s) in respect of the subject matter of the suit and that while the claim made in the suit is being established by legal evidence, the Court passes a decree in favour of the plaintiff and if it is otherwise then dismisses the suit. Thus, the plaintiff is to establish first for having the relief in the suit instituted by him that his suit as framed is maintainable and if same is not established then generally the Court is not required to go for adjudication of other contentions making which relief has been sought in the suit. Law as in Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the plaintiff to give clear description of the land in suit so that the land in suit is identifiable. In the instant case, it is seen that the particulars of the land as in schedule 'Ga' to the plaint is vague and unspecified. In that state of the matter it is clear that the plaintiffs have sought for declaration of title in respect of unspecified, vague and undivided land. If the land in suit is vague, unspecified and that relief sought is in respect of undivided portion of land of particular plot(s), in that case suit seeking mere declaration of title is not maintainable. In this regard, reference may be made to the case of Tayeb Ali vs. Abdul Khaleque and others reported in 43 DLR (AD) 87. Since plaintiffs' suit was not maintainable as they filed a mere declaratory suit in respect of unspecified as well as undivided portion of the land and, as such, even if any adjudication is made as regard the relief sought as to the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 206 of 1976 would be of no purpose since in the absence of seeking consequential relief of recovery of possession mere declaration of title as regard the land described in the schedule 'Ga' cannot be allowed, as because the land as regard which declaration of title has been sought is vague and unspecified as well as relief has been sought as to land of undivided part of the plots mentioned in schedule 'Ga'</u>

16. In the background of the discussions made herein-above we find merit in the appeal.

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs.

End.
